source_group_count.source: All four input readers allocate emission_sourcegroup[101], indexed by internal group index.

source_group_label.source: WriteLogFiles.LogfileGralCoreInfo indexes DecayRate by the external label; ProgramDeclarations initializes DecayRate as double[102]. Valid array indices are 0..101.
source_group_label.supersedes: The native DecayRate boundary supersedes earlier source-only suggestions that byte-sized labels through 255 are usable end to end. Historical source-review notes are retained unchanged.
source_group_label.original_failure_stack: System.IndexOutOfRangeException in ProgramWriters.LogfileGralCoreInfo; optimized Release trace points to method entry, while the last emitted line is Computing pollutant NOx and source inspection identifies DecayRate[sg].
source_group_label.alias_evidence: Byte truncation of labels above 255 is a source-level additional risk. Native labels 1/257 produce no concentration output because the logging array fails first; native aliasing was not reproduced.

missing_receptor.qualification: All variants report the missing receptor input. Original dictionary writes zero total concentration; compare actual figures in missing_receptor_comparisons. This is excluded from valid-input performance results.
missing_receptor.supersedes: The earlier source-only D03 assessment in qa/final_review_notes.json is superseded by this native diagnostic.

direct_writer.qualification: Reflection directly initializes arrays and dictionaries, bypassing input readers and byte particle-label storage. Its index/label 300 success does not prove native group or label support.

method: Recorded outputs only; concentration and deposition metrics are separate; measured-repeat pairs exclude warmups and invalid boundary inputs; unchanged payload hashes avoid decoding.

qualifications: Direct writer/internal-key tests do not establish input-reader support for the same numeric labels or group counts.
Boundary and missing-input diagnostics are excluded from performance evidence even if a process exits successfully.
Concentration and deposition exactness may be combined, but relative L1 is never combined across their different quantities.
The existing benchmark compares repeats to warmup; this report independently compares measured repeats only.
